mission: Orbit over Veranthos. Blue-green oceans, temperate forests, beautiful. Scan data contradicts the beauty — weather patterns not following rotation, vegetation defying sunlight, ocean currents reversed. The seal boundary visible in Force-perception as a membrane; beyond it the wound, gravitational. Desh's sensor confirmation lands the tactical fact: Veraine's ship is on the surface at the valley coordinates — already there.
why_now: PP25 payoff. The destination promised since Chapter 3 arrives in the viewport. The chapter has to deliver the beauty-as-symptom that the remaining book will unpack ring by ring.
conflict: The wrongness from orbit is dense enough to flatten Ben's Force-sense. Professional assessment runs in parallel with visceral dread. The planet is the thing the book has been describing for twenty chapters, and none of the descriptions prepared him for the shape of it.
turning_point: The seal boundary visible in the Force as a membrane, a pressure change. Inside it, the world is wrong. Outside it, almost normal. The boundary is failing, and patches of wrongness bleed through.
opening_hook: Ben presses his hand against the viewport as Veranthos fills the frame — blue-green oceans, temperate forests, beautiful. The beauty is the first warning.
closing_hook: Desh's sensor-sweep confirms Veraine's ship already on the surface at the valley coordinates. No approach time left to spend.
emotional_trajectory: Awed dread -> the wrongness made planetary -> urgent tactical alarm

stakes.personal: Ben facing the source of everything he has been feeling since Chapter 1
stakes.interpersonal: The group's reactions to Veranthos reveal their final emotional states before the endgame
stakes.external: Veraine is already at the wound

setting: Aboard the Steady Returns — orbit over Veranthos
sensory_details: Veranthos from space: lush, blue-green, inviting; scan data contradicting the eye — weather patterns not tracking rotation, vegetation defying sunlight, ocean currents reversed; the Force on scan: the seal membrane visible as a pressure shimmer in perception; beyond it the wound, immense, pulling, silent
action_beats: Ben presses his hand against the viewport as Veranthos fills the frame — beautiful, blue-green, wrong
Desh reads scan data aloud: weather patterns contradicting rotation, vegetation defying sunlight, ocean currents reversing
Desh zooms the sensor display to valley coordinates and confirms Veraine's ship is already on the surface
promises_paid: The primary wound site will be physically visited (PP25)
The wound site has physical presence (PP18)
notes: The chapter's load-bearing image is the beauty-as-symptom — Veranthos lush and temperate, the eye deceived before the scan tells the truth. Anti-pattern: do not describe the ruined world; describe the apparently unruined one and let the data contradict it. Diagnostic-voice trap — Ben should not, in this scene, narrate the seal boundary as concept. He feels the pressure, sees the membrane on scan, registers the wound's pull; the interpretation stays in his body.
